newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed, look to Brazil for support.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed, look to Brazil for support.

text.p: Argentine bonds were mixed late morning Monday as a strong underlying tone failed to prevent some losses after the release of a strong U.S. National Association of Purchasing Manager's index.
"There is not much going on but the market has a strong tone," said a trader.
Prices opened higher but were knocked slightly by the NAPM index which came in at 57.1 in May, compared with 54.2 a month earlier.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at 93-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.05 to 116.40.
Another trader said the market looked strong as high hopes of Brazi's global bond offering and Brady exchange this week maintained an upbeat mood.
In addition, the trader said uncertainty in Europe on the left-wing victory in France's election was buoying the dollar which in turn underpinned Argentine assets.
